segments.text: So my topic today is Explainable and Reliable AI, Comparing Deep Learning with Adaptive Resonance.

segments.text: such as its untrustworthiness because it's unexplainable and its unreliability because it experiences catastrophic forgetting.

segments.text: The article explains how adaptive resonance overcomes these problems, indeed, overcomes 17 problems of deep learning and outlines a blueprint for achieving autonomous adaptive intelligence.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: The article is part of a Frontiers in Neuro-Robotics special issue about explainable AI, whose editors wrote, and I quote, though deep learning is the main pillar of current AI techniques and is ubiquitous in basic science and real world applications, it is also flagged by AI researchers for its black box problem.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: It is easy to fool.

segments.text: and it also cannot explain how it makes a prediction or decision.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: In other words, deep learning is not trustworthy.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: No life or death decision, such as a medical or financial decision, can confidently be made based upon a deep learning prediction.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: Deep learning uses the back propagation algorithm
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: for learning how to predict output vectors in response to input vectors.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: That propagation was based on perceptron learning principles that Frank Rosenblatt started to introduce in the 1950s.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: It has a complicated history, which Juergen Schmidhuber beautifully reviewed in an article from this year.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: Major contributors include Shinichi Omari, Paul Werbos, and David Parker.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: Perhaps one would say that it reached its modern form with simulated applications in Paul's 1974 paper before being popularized 12 years later by Rummel, Hart, Hinton, and Williams.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: Here's a schematic of a back propagation circuit reprinted from a survey article by Gail Carpenter of neural network models.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: In it,
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: Information flows feed forward from an input stage to an output stage.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: Learning is supervised by an external teacher who on each trial defines a target or desired output.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: The teaching signal is the error or mismatch between the actual and the target outputs.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: So the algorithm uses an artifice called weight transport, which physically lifts the weights from here and moves them there so that they can be used to control learning.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: Well, this is clearly a non-local operation as well as being clearly
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: non-biological.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: Backpropagation learns through slow learning, which means that the adaptive weights change just a little to reduce error on each learning trial.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: That requires many trials, that is to say many repetitions of the whole database to learn, possibly hundreds or thousands of trials.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: This is to be contrasted with fast learning,
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: where adaptive weights zero error signals on each trial, just as we can learn a face that we see just once and remember it for a long time.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: If backprop tried to use fast learning, it would become wildly unstable.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: Catastrophic forgetting also occurs in backprop, so that during any learning trial, an unpredictable part of its learned memory can unexpectedly collapse.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: So deep learning, which is based on backpropagation, is thus neither reliable nor trustworthy.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: But why is this?
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: One reason is that all inputs are processed by a shared set of learned weights.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: The algorithm cannot selectively buffer learned weights that are still predictably useful.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: In particular, there's no attention mechanism.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: This problem occurs in any learning algorithm whose shared weight updates follow the gradient of the error in response to the current batch of data points while ignoring past batches.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: There have been multiple efforts to fix back propagation.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: One is to selectively slow learning on the weights important for learning by optimizing parameters using the Bayes rule, as Kirkpatrick et al.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: suggested a few years ago.

segments.text: But that assumes an omniscient observer who can discover and alter the important weights, as well as non-local computations, such as the Bayesian computation.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02

segments.text: I view them as adding epicycles to ameliorate a fundamental flaw in the model, which to me is reminiscent of adding epicycles to correct problems in the Ptolemaic model of the solar system.

segments.text: As we all know, the Copernical model that we now accept didn't require epicycles.

segments.text: as Gail Carpenter and I showed in the 1980s.

segments.text: The importance of this issue becomes clear when we realize that erroneous cues can accidentally be incorporated into a code when our interactions with the environment is simple and will only become evident when our environmental expectations become more demanding.

segments.text: then within the bounds of the prototype, if you also have a bottom-up feature, you have two excitatory against one inhibitory, and those features can be selected, gain amplified and synchronized to start focusing attention on this critical feature pattern, while outlier features, the ones that aren't within the prototype, only have one excitation against one inhibition,
